title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1966-01-08

ai_review.summary: Soundboard tape with modest mic issues but a historically thrilling early‑Dead set highlighted by Death Don't Have No Mercy and youthful Jerry Garcia.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard capture that suffers from occasional microphone problems, yet it remains surprisingly listenable for a 1966 source and offers great historical value. Musically the show delivers raw blues energy, with standout performances of “Death Don't Have No Mercy,” “I’m A Hog For You,” “Caution (Do Not Stop)” and “King Bee,” plus memorable banter including a goofy rendition of the National Anthem. Overall the set is celebrated for its early‑Dead vibe despite a few chaotic moments at the start and finish.

ai_rating.rationale: 14 reviews, most 5‑star with detailed praise of the performance and only minor technical complaints; average star rating ≈4.2 supports a strong positive assessment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers note mic problems, occasional drop‑outs, and a cut‑off ending on “Death Don't Have No Mercy," but many also describe the tape as surprisingly clear and easy to listen given its age.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A raw, energetic early‑Dead set with chaotic opening and closing tracks, strong blues numbers in the middle, and plenty of stage banter that captures the Acid Test atmosphere.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Young Jerry’s guitar work is described as adorable and his tone on “I'm A Hog For You” praised.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s pole‑climbing antics and goofy National Anthem performance are highlighted.
band_member_comments.Keys: First audible keyboard appears on “Death Don't Have No Mercy,” noted as a historic moment.
